name: Personality and Character
blurb: Mô tả người, thói quen, thái độ

words.definitionEn: fond of company; sociable
words.example: Her gregarious nature made her the life of every party.

words.definitionEn: showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise
words.example: A meticulous planner, he double-checked every aspect of the project.

words.definitionEn: showing a selfless concern for the well-being of others
words.example: Her altruistic decision to work in a remote clinic inspired many volunteers.

words.meaningVi: tự mãn, thỏa mãn với bản thân
words.definitionEn: showing uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's achievements
words.example: After years of success, the manager grew complacent and ignored market changes.

words.definitionEn: eager or quick to argue, quarrel, or fight
words.example: His pugnacious attitude alienated even his closest colleagues.

words.definitionEn: exercising a compelling charm that inspires devotion in others
words.example: A charismatic leader can unite people behind a shared vision.

words.meaningVi: kiên cường, có khả năng phục hồi
words.definitionEn: able to recover quickly from difficult conditions
words.example: Resilient individuals often turn setbacks into opportunities for growth.

words.definitionEn: wishing to do one's work or duty thoroughly and carefully
words.example: A conscientious employee always meets deadlines and produces high-quality work.

words.definitionEn: wanting to avoid activity or exertion; lazy
words.example: His indolent cousin spent the entire summer watching television.

words.definitionEn: dealing with things sensibly and realistically
words.example: We need a pragmatic approach to solve this budget crisis.

words.meaningVi: đồng cảm, thấu hiểu cảm xúc người khác
words.definitionEn: showing an ability to understand and share the feelings of another
words.example: An empathetic teacher can sense when a student is struggling emotionally.

words.meaningVi: thất thường, dễ thay đổi (tính cách hoặc tình huống)
words.definitionEn: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse
words.example: Her volatile temper made it hard for colleagues to approach her.

words.meaningVi: ham học hỏi, tò mò muốn biết
words.definitionEn: curious or inquiring; eager for knowledge
words.example: An inquisitive mind is essential for scientific discovery.

words.definitionEn: persistence in doing something despite difficulty or delay in achieving success
words.example: Her perseverance in the face of repeated failures eventually led to a breakthrough.

words.meaningVi: ẩn dật, thích sống tách biệt
words.definitionEn: avoiding the company of other people; solitary
words.example: The reclusive author rarely gave interviews or attended public events.

words.definitionEn: having an exaggerated sense of one's own importance or abilities
words.example: His arrogant remark offended everyone in the meeting.

words.meaningVi: ăn nói lưu loát, rõ ràng
words.definitionEn: having or showing the ability to speak fluently and coherently
words.example: The articulate candidate impressed the interviewers with her clear reasoning.

words.meaningVi: bốc đồng, hành động theo cảm tính
words.definitionEn: acting or done without forethought, on a sudden urge
words.example: Impulsive decisions often lead to regret later.

words.meaningVi: kiên trì, bền bỉ, không từ bỏ
words.definitionEn: holding firmly to something; persistent
words.example: A tenacious negotiator, she refused to accept an unfair deal.

words.meaningVi: nịnh hót, quỵ lụy, đầy tớ
words.definitionEn: having an excessive willingness to serve or please others, often in a submissive way
words.example: His servile manner toward his boss was embarrassing to watch.

words.meaningVi: sành sỏi, tinh tế, có óc phán đoán tốt
words.definitionEn: having or showing good judgment, especially about style or quality
words.example: Discerning readers can spot a poorly structured argument instantly.

words.definitionEn: not pretentious or arrogant; modest
words.example: Despite his fame, the professor remained unassuming and approachable.

words.meaningVi: thù hận, hay nuôi lòng hận thù
words.definitionEn: having or showing a strong or unreasoning desire for revenge
words.example: A vindictive person will hold a grudge for years over a minor offense.

words.meaningVi: chịu đựng, nhẫn nại, không biểu lộ cảm xúc
words.definitionEn: enduring pain or hardship without showing feelings or complaining
words.example: He remained stoic even after learning about the devastating loss.

words.meaningVi: nhiệt tình, hăng hái, cuồng nhiệt
words.definitionEn: having great energy or enthusiasm for a cause or activity
words.example: The zealous volunteer worked tirelessly to support the charity.

words.definitionEn: having a friendly and pleasant manner
words.example: Her amiable nature makes her a popular colleague in the office.

words.definitionEn: truthful and straightforward; frank
words.example: In a candid interview, the CEO admitted the company's past mistakes.

words.definitionEn: having or showing careful and persistent effort
words.example: A diligent student always completes assignments on time and thoroughly.

words.definitionEn: unassuming in the estimation of one's abilities or achievements
words.example: Despite his Nobel Prize, he remained remarkably modest about his contributions.

words.definitionEn: eager or enthusiastic about something
words.example: She is a keen observer of human behaviour, which helps her in negotiations.

words.definitionEn: having a strong desire to do something, not easily discouraged
words.example: His determined effort to improve his English led to an IELTS band 8.

words.definitionEn: deviating from conventional or normal behaviour, especially in a way that is odd or whimsical
words.example: The artist's eccentric style often puzzles critics but delights collectors.

words.definitionEn: having or displaying a passionate intensity
words.example: Fervent supporters of the movement gathered outside the parliament building.

words.definitionEn: friendly and cheerful in manner
words.example: The genial host made everyone feel welcome at the party.

words.definitionEn: arrogantly superior and disdainful
words.example: His haughty tone alienated many of his colleagues in the meeting.

words.definitionEn: treating all rivals or disputants equally; fair and just
words.example: A judge must remain impartial to ensure a fair trial.

words.definitionEn: affected by lethargy; sluggish and apathetic
words.example: After a heavy lunch, many employees feel lethargic and unproductive.

words.definitionEn: stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or chosen course of action
words.example: Despite clear evidence, he remained obstinate and refused to admit his error.

words.definitionEn: not easily upset or excited; calm and peaceful
words.example: Her placid temperament helps her handle stressful situations with ease.

words.definitionEn: acting or done without careful consideration of the consequences
words.example: A rash decision during the negotiation cost the company millions.

words.definitionEn: friendly and welcoming to guests or strangers
words.example: People in rural areas are often more hospitable than those in big cities.

words.definitionEn: inclined to give way to others; compliant or submissive
words.example: A yielding personality can sometimes be mistaken for weakness in negotiations.

words.definitionEn: having a strong desire for success, power, or achievement
words.example: Ambitious individuals often set high goals and work tirelessly to achieve them.

words.definitionEn: feeling or appearing casually calm and relaxed; not showing anxiety or interest
words.example: His nonchalant response to the crisis surprised everyone in the team.

words.definitionEn: optimistic or positive, especially in a difficult situation
words.example: Despite the economic downturn, the investor remained sanguine about the recovery.

words.definitionEn: reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little
words.example: The taciturn professor rarely spoke outside his lectures, but his writing was profound.

words.meaningVi: vô đạo đức, không có nguyên tắc
words.definitionEn: having or showing no moral principles; dishonest or unfair
words.example: Unscrupulous businessmen often exploit loopholes in the law for personal gain.

words.definitionEn: able to adapt or be adapted to many different functions or activities
words.example: A versatile employee can handle tasks ranging from customer service to data analysis.

words.definitionEn: showing quick and inventive verbal humour
words.example: Her witty remarks during the debate made the audience laugh while still proving her point.

words.definitionEn: having an obstinately uncooperative attitude towards authority or discipline
words.example: The recalcitrant student refused to follow any classroom rules, disrupting the lesson.
